notes: The ship's floor plan inside its hull: the outside's plan (data/definitions/ship.json, the owner's plan v7, built at 46 m on PRD #10) split into the rooms, the walkway and what is left out, the inside step of the owner's loop of 2026-10-19. Read by tools/props/scene/ship_floor.py, which measures every room's size and section from the hull itself (tools/props/library/inside/ship_outline.py), so no size here can drift from the hull.
Frame as the ship plan's, built metres: y back from the nose spike's tip, x across (starboard positive, the side ring's side), z up from the ground the ship stands on.

People keep their size at 46 m: doors stay 0.9 x 2.0 m and rooms take a person's ceiling; only the hull's lengths grow. The fix-ship-rooms branch scaled every room 1.5 times instead (ceilings 3 to 5 m, a 1.8 m walkway): replaced by this plan.

Sizes and order come from the hull and the story: the cockpit under the nose windows, navigation beside it, the crew's quarters and galley together, storage beside the ship's lock so cargo comes in through the one hatch, the engine room aft over the engines, the walkway joining them all.
made: 2026-10-19, the ship lead, from plan v7 at 46 m; navigation merged into the cockpit (the owner, 2026-10-21, on the hangar's plan: "changed cockpit to cockpit and nav ; and removed nav"; from tail to nose the engine room, shiplock (west) and galley (east), storage (west) and quarters (east), the walkway down the middle, at the nose one room 'cockpit and nav'; rooms fill the hull width)
deck_why: the main deck's floor over the ground: plan v7's 1.6 m drawn times 1.5, the height the hull's side ring is built on (fix-ship-hull)
lining_why: the hull's frame and lining between its outside and a room's wall
floor_depth_why: the deck's structure under a floor: the hull's keel must lie at least this far under it
head_why: a person's height over a floor: a room is as wide as the hull is at its floor and at this height, the narrower
ceiling_why: a room's clear height on the one deck; the hull's space over it (2.0 to 2.9 m clear from y 22 to 34) is the service space

walkway.for: the corridor joining every room, cockpit to engine room, down the ship's middle line
